These satellites closely tracked military installations and vital facilities like the Jamnagar refinery owned by Reliance. By adjusting their orbits, they optimized their capacity to observe military activities, especially during a brief four-day period of heightened tensions.

headline: UP polls: SP springs surprise by naming 5 candidates; 2 seats were on Congress wishlist
excerpt: The Samajwadi Party has revealed its first list of candidates for the upcoming 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The party retained its sitting MLAs while aiming to maintain its electoral strategy focusing on specific community representation. Simultaneously, negotiations with the Congress over seat-sharing continue, revealing significant differences between both parties.

headline: Cops stop Mehbooba‘s Sheshnag trek amid BRO construction row
excerpt: Concerns are mounting among political leaders, notably PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti, regarding the construction activities near Sheshnag Lake. Environmental advocates and Congress members underscore the area's ecological sensitivity. Detractors warn that development could endanger local ecosystems, revealing a broader conflict between aspirations for growth and the need for environmental conservation.

excerpt: MacKenzie Scott has donated $62 million to the marine conservation organization Blue Ventures for their 2030 goals. headline: India’s space economy projected to rise to $40-45 billion by 2036: Science minister
excerpt: India's space economy is expected to significantly increase, rising from nearly $9 billion to $40-45 billion by 2036. This growth will largely be driven by private companies contributing to the space sector. Space, Science and Technology Minister Jitendra Singh highlighted key reforms that spurred this transformation, including the establishment of New Space India Limited. The minister urged greater corporate involvement in scientific research and emphasised the importance of indigenous capabilities.

excerpt: In North Carolina, Jennifer and Lane Tredway donated development rights to protect their 55-acre farm. This conservation easement will ensure the land remains agricultural and untouched by future development. The farm, known as Two Paths Farm, is situated in an area experiencing rapid urban expansion. excerpt: NATO chief Mark Rutte said Monday the alliance would defend against threats in space when asked about German media reports that Russia may be preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite. excerpt: Haitians are hailing the Bukele method. Citizens of the Americas’ poorest nation cheering the Salvadoran president’s ’shoot first, ask questions later’ method of dealing with the gangs that have overrun their country the past six years. excerpt: Speaking with FRANCE 24's Jennie Shin, sports presenter and journalist Thando Sibiya explains that the decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport to reinstate Senegal as winner of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations "from a jurisprudence perspective or creating precedent, it is going to be good in the books of sports law, because if every single decision of a referee is taken to a court of law all the time, it really tampers with the quality, governance and legitimacy of the game".

headline: Senegal regain AFCON title on appeal at Morocco's expense
excerpt: Senegal on Tuesday regained their Africa Cup of Nations title after winning an appeal at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the decision by the Confederation of African Football to declare Morocco the winners following a chaotic final in January. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.

headline: Gunmen hold 25 people hostage at supermarket in Colombia's Cartagena

excerpt: France's former president Nicolas Sarkozy and his wife, singer Carla Bruni-Sarkozy, are set to be tried in 2027 on charges of "criminal conspiracy with intent to commit fraud" as well as benefitting from witness tampering. excerpt: Senegal were reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners on Tuesday after the Court of Arbitration for Sport upheld their appeal against being stripped of the title. excerpt: USA: Powerful waves and king tides destroyed part of a pier in Pacifica, south of San Francisco, on Wednesday. In Marin County, authorities issued a temporary evacuation order and urged people to stay away from the beach.

headline: Spanish economist de Cos to succeed Lagarde as head of ECB
excerpt: Spanish monetary economist Pablo Hernandez de Cos on Thursday was set to replace France's Christine Lagarde as the new head of the European Central Bank (ECB). headline: Lost homes, stolen freedom: National Book Award winners on exile and imprisonment
excerpt: Two books about losing everything have just won America's most prestigious literary honours. Hannah Lillith Assadi took the National Book Award for fiction for "Paradiso 17", a novel inspired by her late father, who was driven from Palestine in 1948 during the Nakba. Abdelrahman ElGendy won the non-fiction prize for "Huna", his memoir of six years as a political prisoner in Egypt, arrested at 17 alongside his father. ElGendy couldn't be in New York to collect his award: his visa was denied.

headline: How far-right Vox is winning over young voters ahead of Spain's snap election
excerpt: Spain's Vox party is winning over many young people ahead of the country's snap election on November 29, particularly men. The far-right party is capitalising on the rising cost of living and anti-immigrant sentiment to expand its once-marginal electoral base.

headline: Across Africa: The Scars of South Africa's Soweto Uprising
excerpt: 50 years ago, thousands of young South Africans from Soweto protested against apartheid's stranglehold on their education and the imposition of Afrikaans as a language of instruction. What began as a peaceful protest ended in bloodshed. And men in Northern Benin confront uncomfortable realities about the lives of the women who live and love them. [Archive edition, June 2026]

headline: From leadership crises to tech outages, can corporations rebuild public trust?
excerpt: From cyberattacks to network failures to leadership crises, tech corporations are showing signs of vulnerability. The dramatic resignation and return of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has underscored the potential risk of depending on a single leader, both for the company and the entire AI industry. Meanwhile, global outages at Microsoft and a number of US banks have showcased declining public trust in institutions.

headline: French woman on trial for IS group propaganda tells court she’s ‘ashamed’
excerpt: The trial of Émilie König, one of France's most high-profile Islamic State (IS) group recruits, opened in a Paris court on Thursday with the 41-year-old mother of five apologising to her children, mother and the "French nation" for her actions. König travelled in 2012 to Syria, where she appeared in the jihadist group's propaganda videos. She was repatriated to France in 2022.

headline: Season's eatings! Celebrating Thanksgiving in France
excerpt: This Thursday marks Thanksgiving in the United States, the biggest travel holiday of the year there and arguably the most important on US calendars. But here in France, it's just another day. However, Americans living in Paris do try to capture the Thanksgiving spirit, though it can be tricky to track down the turkeys and pies required. Joining us to discuss how Americans do Thanksgiving in Paris is Cordon Bleu-trained chef and the owner of Boneshaker Donuts, Amanda Bankert.

headline: Madagascar's near-total abortion ban puts women's lives at risk
excerpt: November 25 marked the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. Activists argue that tackling gender-based violence also means addressing the wider inequalities that put women at risk, including restrictions on reproductive rights. In Madagascar, abortion is almost entirely banned, even in cases of rape, incest or when a woman's life is at risk. FRANCE 24’s Aurélie Kouman reports on the consequences of the country's strict laws, which force thousands of women to seek unsafe, clandestine procedures.

headline: Fighting in eastern Congo forces Ebola workers to evacuate, disrupts outbreak response
excerpt: Escalating fighting in eastern Congo has forced Ebola response workers to leave affected areas and disrupted efforts to contain the deadliest outbreak in the country, health officials and humanitarian workers said Wednesday. Congo’s Ebola outbreak has infected more than 11,700 people and killed more than 5,700 since it was declared in May, according to the latest government data. FRANCE 24's Emmet Livingstone reports from Kinshasa, DR Congo.

headline: Moscow drone incursions: Poland to create no-fly zone at Ukraine border

headline: Émilie König, 'the muse of the Islamic State group' goes on trial in France

On Thursday, Émilie König appears before a special criminal court in Paris, seeking to convince judges that she has been deradicalised. Originally from western France, König spent a decade in Syria and is accused of being one of the Islamic State group's most active French propagandists. Charged with criminal association with a terrorist organisation, she maintains that she has no blood on her hands.

In calling the snap election, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez is hoping the housing issue can galvanise his left-wing base.

headline: 'As humans we feel spiritually homeless': Turkish author Ece Temelkuran on belonging

This feeling of "spiritual homelessness" is something she explores in her latest book, "Nation of Strangers: Rebuilding Home in the 21st Century". Most of all, she highlights the importance of human connection: "In survival mode (...) you live on the kindness of others."
